body: It seems OpenHarmony and Android are very similar in terms of exporting.
Changes looks fine to me. I have not looked at platform code in depth, and do not have a device to test it.

As far as the export process is concerned, there is no problem exporting **unsigned** apps, but there will be an error when exporting signed apps (probably an issue with `hvigorw`). Additionally, the requirements for directly exporting a signed app are a bit demanding and not well documented. Here are my summary of the requirements (I'm using Command Line Tools version 5.1.0, maybe I should try an earlier version, which can be found on the [Chinese page](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/cn/download/command-line-tools-for-hmos)): 1. It requires that the length of `storePassword` and `keyPassword` must be an **even** number **not less** than `32`; 2. It requires that there must be a directory named `material` in the directory where the `.p12` file is located; 3. The `material` directory should contain subdirectories named `ac`, `ce`, and `fd`. I'm not sure how to generate these files manually, so directly exporting the signed app fails. ``` > hvigor ERROR: Failed :entry:default@SignHap... > hvigor ERROR: 00303119 Configuration Error Error Message: Signing failed: Signing materials /opt/godot/test/key/material/fd is illegal!. At file: /opt/godot/test/A/build-profile.json5 * Try the following: > Ensure signing materials /opt/godot/test/key/material/fd is correct > Re-execute sign your appp/atomic service automatically：clear the signingConfigs field in the /opt/godot/test/A/build-profile.json5 file and go to Project Structure > Project > Signing Configs and apply the signature material > Reconfigure the signature or clear the /opt/godot/test/key folder and perform signing again. > hvigor ERROR: BUILD FAILED in 9 s 943 ms ``` A feasible solution (and there are no restrictions as above): first export the unsigned app, and then sign it using the following command (please replace the value of the parameter in the command according to the actual situation): ```bash $ java -jar /path/to/command-line-tools/sdk/default/openharmony/toolchains/lib/hap-sign-tool.jar sign-app -keyAlias "sign/key_alias" -signAlg "sign/sign_alg" -mode "localSign" -appCertFile "sign/certpath_file" -profileFile "sign/profile_file" -inFile "/path/to/unsigned.hap" -keystoreFile "sign/store_file" -outFile "hap-signed.hap" -keyPwd "sign/key_password" -keystorePwd "sign/store_password" -signCode "1" ``` Signed release apps can be uploaded to AppGallery Connect and installed on devices that meet the API level (OS version does not seem to matter). But the icon is not showing: Simple projects can be run, I also tried to export [dodge_the_creeps](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/2d/dodge_the_creeps) and [voxel](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/3d/voxel), which can be installed, ~~but cannot be run~~(it may be that the configuration of some environment variables has not taken effect).

I hope this PR will add the following features:
1. Allow custom `versionCode` and `versionName` when exporting.
2. Provide an additional option to [use `hap_sign_tool.jar` for signing](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/cn/doc/harmonyos-guides/ide-command-line-building-app#section103321051433). To use `hvigor` automatic signing, it seems that the conditions in `command-line-tools/hvigor/hvigor-ohos-plugin/src/utils/decipher-util{.d.ts, .js}` need to be met.

It seems that some tools in **command-line-tools** do not take into account the situation where the path contains spaces.

It is recommended to explain this issue in the documentation and advise users not to include spaces in the path when exporting.

Others look good.
